Hey, we had a promo credit on our account—can you tell me if it’s still there, whether it was used on our March 2027 bill, and how much the Mar 1-15 usage line on that bill is?

{"name": "payments-and-credits", "steps": "Failed payment
1. Get the invoice, the decline code, and when it failed with the timezone they used (`ask_developer` once for what's missing). Convert the time to UTC.
2. `search_knowledge` for the payment-processor incident procedure and for incident status cards for payment failures around that date (e.g. "INC card payments failing <month year>"). Read each card's window (UTC).
3. Inside a published window (the boundaries count as inside): the time decides, not the decline code. Name the incident, say the payment will be retried automatically and when retries complete, that they need do nothing, and that no late fees apply. No case. If this incident's notice gives no completion date, work it out from the usual schedule: search the earlier payment-processor incident notices, compare each window's end with its "last retries completed" date, apply that gap to this window's end, and say it is based on the usual schedule.
4. Outside every window, failed again after retries completed, or charged twice after retries: open the case the routing page names with invoice, decline code and failure time.
5. Card changes: Support never takes or repeats card numbers and doesn't change payment methods. Point them to Console billing settings; no case. If they shared a number, tell them not to send card details.

Overdue, late fees, suspension
- Use the current collections/dunning pages (check the effective year and whether the account pays by card or by invoice) and the account's invoice status from the console. Payments failed in an incident window are not overdue until retries finish.

Credit balance and expiry
1. `account_overview`: quote the balance from `credits` (the credit ledger), the balance and expiry date of each grant, not only the total. Confirm with `search_knowledge` which table policy says to quote if anything looks inconsistent.
2. Cash-out, refund of credits, restoring an expired credit, or another exception: explain the policy, promise nothing, and route the ask as the credit-ledger/routing pages say. Promo or workshop codes: follow their page (usually no case)."}

{"query": "March 2027 invoice usage line Mar 1-15 invoice period line item billing invoice periods credit application date", "results": [{"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-22", "text": "| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |
Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.
## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.
## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.
The 2027 price book takes effect for usage from 1 March 2027: February 2027 and earlier usage is rated on the 2026 price book, and March 2027 usage onward on the 2027 price book.
## Credits and the close
Credit notes issued before BD4 are applied to the invoice being issued; later credit notes are applied to the next invoice. The credit ledger shows the date each one was applied."}, {"source": "confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/support-console-record-format-changes-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Console: Record Format Changes (April 2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-29", "text": "- A write or query on those tables that still sends `account_id` fails with an unknown-field error. Read-only tables keep `account_id`.
## Billing timezone
- Accounts have a `billing_timezone` (an IANA name such as `America/Los_Angeles`; `UTC` unless set).
- Which billing month and invoice line a request belongs to is set by Finance's invoice period rules; see Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods (Finance shared drive).
## Case priority
- A case can only be set to `escalated` with a `priority` of `normal` or `urgent`, whether it is escalated when first inserted or by a later update. A draft case can still leave it empty.
- Which priority Support sets on a billing handoff was announced by Dev Patel in #support on 2027-03-30.
